quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your riding ability:

options.text: Once you reach the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking alcohol. Your riding skills get worse well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Is usually too warm to wear.
Should not be worn while riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. It protects you in a crash and helps prevent dehydration in warm weather. Modern motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: When another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone drank 8 drinks 4 hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the drinks consumed. 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes position within their lane based on conditions.
Stays in one spot in their lane.
Weaves within the lane to be seen.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within their lane based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders can use three different positions in their lane. Choose the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and don't use it again.
Release the front brake and quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear without slowing down enough, the:

options.text: Motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: When riding on rough surfaces, you should:
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, hold the handlebars firmly to keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times and position yourself where oncoming drivers can see you best. Keep space around you to avoid hazards. Do not rely only on eye contact with drivers.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Keep your eyes focused only 15 feet in front of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, tell other drivers what you plan to do, keep space around your motorcycle, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to daytime, what should a rider NOT do?

options.text: Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Stay flexible with your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straight road?

options.text: It is easier than braking on a straight road.
It is harder than braking on a straight road.
It is done safely by using only the front brake.
It is done safely by using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver burns alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Time is the only thing that reduces alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by gradually closing the throttle, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road. Do not brake, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, make yourself as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How many drinks must you have before you feel alcohol's effects?
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding while under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which item does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Which riding formation keeps a group of riders closest together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets a group stay close while giving each rider safe space. Use single-file for curves, turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver can see you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers notice objects best when they appear in the middle of the mirror.

questions.question: What can reduce your risk of a crash?

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Only watch five feet ahead while riding.
Always be prepared to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be prepared to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger in a sidecar, how should you adjust your braking?

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Brake more gently to protect the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down sooner than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger in the sidecar adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. You will need more distance to stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move to the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest option is to get the tailgater in front of you. Change lanes when safe and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the correct settings for the extra weight.
